target_name: Capex Against Net Short-Term Funding Position
rationale: The expression is internally consistent (heavy capex × negative net near-term liquidity → low returns) and netting cash against short debt firm-by-firm is a defensible economic re-specification rather than a rank average, but it remains a conditioner swap within the already-productive capx/ppent × short-funding family, so the incremental information is modest.

This is essentially the mirrored corner of the archive's accepted "Aged Capital With Liquidity Firepower" using the identical two state variables with both legs sign-flipped — the non-symmetry of the rank product makes it technically a different portfolio but not a substantively new mechanism, and the young-PP&E leg is largely a proxy for recent asset growth, so a negative result would be uninformative and a positive one near-redundant.

target_name: Capital Deepening Backed by Cash Coverage
rationale: Capital-for-labor substitution is a genuinely new construct here and the netting of headcount growth is a real design choice, but the expected positive sign sits in direct tension with the natural direction of the dominant leg (gross PP&E growth is a well-documented negative predictor, as the archive's own ppegt-growth signals confirm), so the sign prior is fragile and rests entirely on the emp subtraction and the coverage conditioner.

The first leg is close to a direct rediscovery of the published net-debt-issuance/liability-growth anomaly (and overlaps the archive's GROWTH(lt) − GROWTH(ppegt) signal), while the second leg (capx/depreciation, already tested at ~zero) carries a natural direction opposite to the expected positive sign, so the proposal mixes a known effect with a leg whose sign prior contradicts the hypothesis.

The diagnosis of why the gen-3 intangibles signal had an inverted FMB slope (a contrarian sales-growth conditioner) is sound and the replacement conditioner is correctly signed, but the result is a two-deflator re-specification of the gen-1 intangibles × weak-cash-flow signal that already delivered −4.7% alpha at t = −3.9, so it risks being a cosmetic variant rather than a new mechanism.

target_name: Investment at Own-History Peak Without Coverage
rationale: This is the gen-1 "Capex Without Debt-Service Capacity" signal with a single operator swapped (IND_RANK → TS_RANK over five annual observations), i.e., a minimal variant whose within-firm leg is also coarsely discretized at annual frequency, so it is too incremental to justify a separate test slot despite the legitimate underlying design question.
